Quick Check 4.1 — Separation vs Overlap Logic You wrote by checking whether the segments are NOT separated. Why is it easier to check for separation instead of directly checking for overlap? A. Separation is faster to compute B. Overlap has many sub-cases (partial overlap, containment, touching at endpoint) but separation has only two simple conditions C. Python can only check inequality, not equality D. Separation works in 2D but overlap doesn't

fragments.text: Answer: B. There are many ways two segments can overlap: one could be inside the other, they could partially overlap, or they could just touch at an endpoint. But there are only two ways they can be completely separate: one is entirely to the left of the other, or entirely to the right. Checking for separation and then negating is much simpler.

Quick Check 6.1 — Dimension Decomposition To check if two rectangles intersect in 2D, you checked whether their projections overlap on BOTH axes. What happens if you only check one axis? A. You get the correct answer for squares, but not rectangles B. You might say they intersect when they actually don't — projections can overlap on one axis while the rectangles are side by side on the other C. You miss some valid intersections D. It works fine for 2D — one axis is enough

fragments.text: Answer: B. Picture two rectangles that are at the same height but far apart left-to-right. Their y-ranges overlap, but they do not touch. You need BOTH axes to overlap for an actual intersection.
